## Purpose and Entry Points
Bettercap is a Go security-research framework for reconnaissance, interception, spoofing, scanning, and attacks across Ethernet/IP, Wi‑Fi, BLE, CAN, and wireless HID. The CLI process begins at `main.go`, initializes platform-aware core behavior in `core/core.go`, and creates an interactive/scriptable operating session in `session/session.go`.

## Session, Commands, and Module Lifecycle
The session layer is the central control plane: it parses commands, manages environment and routing state, loads module parameters, and dispatches module lifecycle operations. Key boundaries are `session/command_handler.go`, `session/module_handler.go`, and `session/session_setup.go`. Modules are registered through `modules/modules.go`; each module exposes capabilities to the shared session rather than owning the application process.

## Core Network and Device Model
`network/` supplies cross-module representations and OS-specific access to network interfaces, LAN endpoints, gateways, Wi‑Fi, BLE, CAN, HID, packet capture, and manufacturer metadata. Important paths are `network/net.go`, `network/lan_endpoint.go`, and `network/pcap.go`. Platform implementations split at build/runtime boundaries, including `network/net_linux.go`, `network/net_darwin.go`, and `network/net_windows.go`; this isolates OS networking differences from higher-level modules.

## Packet, Routing, and Traffic Manipulation
Protocol encoding/parsing is concentrated in `packets/`, including Ethernet-adjacent and higher-level protocols such as 802.11, ARP, DHCPv6, mDNS, NTLM, MySQL, and TCP/UDP (`packets/dot11.go`, `packets/arp.go`, `packets/tcp.go`). Routing updates are abstracted in `routing/route.go` with per-OS update implementations. Firewall/redirection functions form a privileged integration boundary for interception and transparent proxying: `firewall/firewall.go`, `firewall/redirection.go`, and OS-specific firewall files.

## Reconnaissance and Radio/Bus Modules
Modules implement operational features against the shared network model. Major acquisition paths include IP discovery and probing (`modules/net_recon/net_recon.go`, `modules/net_probe/net_probe.go`), packet sniffing and protocol extraction (`modules/net_sniff/net_sniff.go`, `modules/net_sniff/net_sniff_parsers.go`), Wi‑Fi scanning/injection/handshake capture (`modules/wifi/wifi.go`, `modules/wifi/wifi_recon.go`, `modules/wifi/wifi_inject.go`), BLE reconnaissance (`modules/ble/ble_recon.go`), CAN decoding/injection/fuzzing (`modules/can/can.go`, `modules/can/can_dbc.go`), and HID reconnaissance/injection (`modules/hid/hid.go`, `modules/hid/hid_inject.go`).

## Interception, Spoofing, and Application Proxies
MITM-oriented modules alter network behavior through ARP, DNS, NDP, and DHCPv6 spoofing, backed by the firewall/routing boundary: `modules/arp_spoof/arp_spoof.go`, `modules/dns_spoof/dns_spoof.go`, `modules/ndp_spoof/ndp_spoof.go`. Traffic can then traverse packet-, TCP-, HTTP-, HTTPS-, SSH-, or DNS-level proxies. Core proxy implementations include `modules/http_proxy/http_proxy.go`, `modules/https_proxy/https_proxy.go`, and `modules/packet_proxy/packet_proxy_linux.go`. TLS certificate creation/signing is internalized in `tls/cert.go` and `tls/sign.go`.

## Automation, Observability, and Remote Control
JavaScript is an embedded extension boundary used by scripts and proxy/DNS hooks; runtime bindings cover HTTP, filesystem, crypto, random, logging, and data via `js/init.go`, `js/http.go`, and `js/fs.go`. Caplets package reusable command/script environments through `caplets/manager.go` and `modules/caplets/caplets.go`. Events flow from session/module activity into stream views and triggers (`session/events.go`, `modules/events_stream/events_stream.go`, `modules/events_stream/events_triggers.go`). Remote orchestration is provided by REST and WebSocket API support in `modules/api_rest/api_rest.go` and `modules/api_rest/api_rest_ws.go`; the bundled browser UI is served from `modules/ui/ui.go` and static assets under `modules/ui/ui/`.

## Runtime and Delivery Boundaries
The primary runtime is a native Go executable with Unix, Windows, Android, Darwin, Linux, and unsupported-feature variants visible in `core/core_*.go` and module-specific platform files. It interacts directly with host network adapters and specialized Wi‑Fi/BLE/CAN/HID hardware, often requiring OS-level packet capture, routing, and firewall privileges. Container delivery is supported by `Dockerfile` and `Dockerfile.arm64`; CI builds/tests across Linux, macOS, and Windows and publishes deployable images through `.github/workflows/`.
